detailed_descriptions.en: Step into the paws of Hubert , a loyal shepherd navigating the uncharted northern wilderness. In this atmospheric third-person adventure, guide a scattered flock of sheep across gorgeous nature, braving harsh weather, treacherous terrain, and hidden dangers. Hubert blends immersive storytelling with a unique herding gameplay experience, all from the perspective of a devoted working dog. A tale of friendship, bravery, and barking at sheep. THE DOG Meet Hubert, a fluffy and overconfident dog with a nose for trouble. He sees the world through movement, scent, instinct, and curiosity. You experience the journey entirely from Hubert’s perspective, as a devoted working dog learning his place in a quiet world that slowly proves less predictable than it seems. THE BOND Hubert is not alone. By his side is Lily, a sharp-witted kid who just convinced the grumpiest farmer in the valley to give them a job. Their relationship grows through shared routines, small moments, and quiet trust. As the world around them changes, that bond is tested in subtle ways, shaping how Hubert sees the world and why he keeps going. THE HERD Their mission is to herd dozens of mildly chaotic sheep across pastures. Easy, right? Well, not when the sheep have the attention span of a goldfish and the farmer has zero patience. Herding With Heart (and Fur): Commander Hubert is leading a battalion of sheep. A Story Full of Barks and Blunders: Navigate farm life, forge unlikely friendships, and try to stay on the farmer’s good side, or at least out of range of his angry voice. THE WILD Beyond the fence line, the land grows quieter and stranger. There is something in the woods? Something is out there. It is not just a threat, but a call Hubert understands in ways he cannot fully explain. Brush-Painted Charm: Explore a countryside that feels warm and inviting on the surface, yet hides moments of unease, mystery, and the occasional howling at the moon. Warning : This game contains mild mischief, stubborn sheep, and a dog who thinks he’s the main character (He might be right.)
